The document does not describe an analyst-facing complex survey design or specify student sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures. The figures and tables referenced (e.g., unemployment rates, wage gaps, expenditure per student) are presented as descriptive indicator outputs, so no PV-based estimation or replicate variance computation is documented here. For users who access the underlying OECD indicator datasets, the appropriate weighting and variance procedures are expected to be defined in the corresponding Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes (and the OECD Handbook for Internationally Comparative Education Statistics), not in this short country note.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is a system-level country note for Slovenia using the latest available year of indicators from Education at a Glance 2025; it does not define an analytic student sample or inclusion/exclusion criteria for microdata.

data.outcome_summary: Education at a Glance 2025 (Slovenia country note) provides descriptive indicators about the education system, with emphasis on tertiary education. The note reports trends and cross-sectional comparisons such as unemployment rates of 25–34 year-olds by educational attainment, wage gaps by attainment level, participation and progression measures (e.g., age-for-grade in lower secondary, entry routes into tertiary, gender composition of entrants), and tertiary completion and dropout patterns (including pandemic-era changes). It also summarises resource indicators including government expenditure per student by education level and teacher-related inputs such as compulsory instruction time, class size, and the allocation of instruction time to core subjects. The document does not present an assessment design with student-level sampling, plausible values, or an ML modelling pipeline; instead, it points readers to the corresponding Education at a Glance 2025 tables and methodology/technical notes for indicator construction and any underlying data processing.
